title: The ring ℤ/9 — 24 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
The ring ℤ/9. 24 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/z9.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. 21 are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). 3 are proved for every value, on the standard axioms only (propext, Quot.sound; the verifier refuses any other). One further declaration closes by rfl, checked by evaluation, and is not included here, by design. Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 7 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 182 pairs; the theorems fall into 1 strand. Most binding: m9 (12), units (11), orbit (8), B (7), pow9 (5), isUnit (2).

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: imagined.lean, merkaba.lean. Checking this cluster needs 1 file: src/proof/z9.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 24 sealed receipts fold to d64f9352-f528-84ef-ad67-57ae1d3c2b59. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (3, 6, 3, 3, 4, 8, 0). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: demand.lean (6 observed, 2.26 expected, lift 2.65), speed.lean (6 observed, 2.47 expected, lift 2.43), demand3.lean (9 observed, 3.91 expected, lift 2.3). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 2.43 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 35.0% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 14.96; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.56. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 6a9edd0c7e28 (2026-09-15), over 817 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. Fermat’s little theorem — Pierre de Fermat, 1640; Euler’s theorem — Leonhard Euler, 1763; primitive roots — Carl Friedrich Gauss, 1801. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. units_are_six — units = [1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8] record
  2. units_count — units.length = 6 record
  3. hasinv_units — units.all (fun u => (List.range B).any (fun e => m9 (u * e) == 1)) record
  4. hasinv_triad_not — ¬ ([3, 6, 0].any (fun t => (List.range B).any (fun e => m9 (t * e) == 1))) record
  5. selfinv_exactly_one_and_eight — (units.filter (fun u => m9 (u * u) == 1)) = [1, 8] record
  6. euler_units_pow_six — units.all (fun u => pow9 u 6 == 1) record
  7. invpow_is_u_to_the_fifth — units.all (fun u => m9 (u * pow9 u 5) == 1) record
  8. powsum_zero_at_six — m9 ((units.map (fun u => pow9 u 6)).foldl (· + ·) 0) = 6 record
  9. powsum_zero_at_one — m9 ((units.map (fun u => pow9 u 1)).foldl (· + ·) 0) = 0 record
  10. mulperm_iff_unit — (List.range B).all (fun k => ((units.map (fun u => m9 (k * u))).eraseDups.length == units.length) == isUnit k) record
  11. addgen_iff_coprime — (List.range B).all (fun k => (((List.range B).map (fun i => m9 (k * i))).eraseDups.length == B) == isUnit k) record
  12. selfneg_only_zero — ((List.range B).filter (fun d => m9 (2 * d) == 0)) = [0] record
  13. orbit_is_the_six — (List.range 6).map orbit = [1, 2, 4, 8, 7, 5] record
  14. orbit_closes — orbit 6 = orbit 0 record
  15. orbit_distinct — ((List.range 6).map orbit).eraseDups.length = 6 record
  16. orbit_covers_units — ((List.range 6).map orbit).eraseDups.length = units.length record
  17. the_orbit_step_is_read_back_by_its_log — (List.range 6).all (fun k => logOrbit (orbit k) == some k) ∧ units.all (fun u => (logOrbit u).map orbit == some u) record
  18. triad_never_reaches_one — ¬ ((List.range 12).any (fun k => pow9 3 (k + 1) == 1 || pow9 6 (k + 1) == 1)) record
  19. triad_squares_vanish — m9 (3 * 3) = 0 ∧ m9 (6 * 6) = 0 record
  20. add_group — (List.range B).all (fun d => (List.range B).any (fun e => m9 (d + e) == 0)) record
  21. neg_involution — (List.range B).all (fun d => m9 (B - m9 (B - d)) == m9 d) record
  22. orbit_repeats_every_six — ∀ k : Nat, orbit (k + 6) = orbit k record
  23. orbit_is_its_exponent_mod_six — ∀ k : Nat, orbit k = orbit (k % 6) record
  24. the_orbit_step_is_read_back_by_its_log_for_every_k — ∀ k : Nat, logOrbit (orbit k) = some (k % 6) record
